questions.q: Which table stores a customer invoice/transaction in Oracle Fusion Receivables?
questions.explain: RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_ALL stores transaction (invoice, credit memo, debit memo) header information.

questions.q: Why does Fusion model a customer's account (HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS) separately from the customer's underlying identity (HZ_PARTIES)?
options: It doesn't — they are the same table under two names
Because HZ_PARTIES only stores dates, never names
Because Oracle requires every table to have exactly one other related table
Because the same real-world party could, in principle, have more than one account relationship
questions.explain: Separating party identity from account relationship allows one party to potentially have multiple customer accounts.

questions.q: Which column does RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_ALL use to join to HZ_CUST_ACCOUNTS?
What does AR_RECEIVABLE_APPLICATIONS_ALL actually join to, to connect a cash receipt back to a transaction?
options: It cannot be joined to anything else
questions.explain: AR_RECEIVABLE_APPLICATIONS_ALL.APPLIED_PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_ID joins to AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL.PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_ID, not straight to the transaction.

questions.q: What is the Receivables-side equivalent of AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL, the linking table from the Payables chain?
questions.explain: AR_RECEIVABLE_APPLICATIONS_ALL plays the same linking role on Receivables that AP_INVOICE_PAYMENTS_ALL plays on Payables.
